1681: ## DampedMultiplier (whole result)
1682: 
1683: Formalizes the parts of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
1684: (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lemma lines
1685: 803-848, proof lines 850-919) that `DampedNormsHomog` left out: the lower
1686: bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (display at lines 836-841; the
1687: multiplier class and the Laplace domains at lines 826-834), and the smoothing
1688: assertions at the end of the lemma (lines 845-847) and of its proof (lines
1689: 915-917). Read with `E:damped-norm-definitions` (lines 782-793) and
1690: `G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)` (lines 777-778). `DampedNormsHomog`
1691: and `WaveGreen` are unchanged; the extended wrappers are new declarations.
1692: With this module and `DampedNormsHomog`, `WaveGreen`, every assertion of the
1693: lemma except part of its closing smoothing sentence is a Lean conclusion under
1694: `H:homog` with nothing supplied (`damped_homogeneous_norms_full_wave`). The
1695: smoothing sentence is formalized in the narrower reading fixed by Le's
1696: decision 2 for wave L8 (below): spatial smoothing of the covariance only as
1697: the membership of `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)` in the multiplier class (the spectral
1698: identification of `p_eps * Gamma` is not stated), and Gaussian smoothing of
1699: the Green kernel as the multiplier on the transforms of `G_s` in every `d`,
1700: identified with `N_{2,m,S}` in `d = 1` by `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`
1701: and, since wave L9, in `d = 1, 2, 3` by
1702: `WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave` (`full_wave` itself
1703: does not contain that identification). The spectral identification of the
1704: smoothed covariance remains unformalized.

1706: Formalized.
1707: - The lower bounds: `0 <= N_{1,m,S}(theta)` (`N1on_nonneg`, for any measure
1708:   and `a > 0`) and `0 <= N_{2,m,S}(theta)^2` (`N2onSq_nonneg`, for an s-finite
1709:   measure with `int (1+norm(xi)^2)^(-1) dmu < infinity`, `mu{0} = 0`,
1710:   `0 < a < 1`, `theta > 0`, measurable `S`); `damped_multiplier_comparison`
1711:   states the whole display, both bounds with the integrability of the
1712:   integrands, for a general measure (the upper bounds are
1713:   `DampedNormsHomog.N1on_smoothed_mono` and `N2onSq_smoothed_mono`).
1714: - The multiplier class `IsMultiplier` (measurable, values in `[0,1]`; the
1715:   TeX's `m : R^d -> [0,1]` measurable, lines 826-827), closed under products
1716:   (`IsMultiplier.mul`), containing the Gaussian multipliers
1717:   `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)`, `eta >= 0` (`gaussMult`, `isMultiplier_gaussMult`).
1718: - The `N_0` mass sentence (lines 846-847, proof lines 916-917): convolution
1719:   with a probability measure preserves `GreenMass` (`greenMass_conv`), so
1720:   `N_0` is unchanged and equals `theta^(-2)` (`N0_conv`); instantiated with the
1721:   Gaussian `gaussKernel v` and the wave Green measures, `d = 1, 2, 3`
1722:   (`gauss_waveGreen_mass`).
1723: - Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (lines 845-846, proof lines
1724:   915-916): for a finite `G`, the characteristic function of `p * G`
1725:   (`p = gaussKernel v`, `v >= 0`) is `e^(-v norm(xi)^2/2) G hat`
1726:   (`charFun_gaussKernel_conv`), so the product of the transforms is multiplied
1727:   by `e^(-v norm(xi)^2)` (`charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv`). Hence the second
1728:   norm of `p * G` (`N2GreenSq`: `E:damped-norm-definitions` with kernel `K_S`
1729:   and `G_s hat` the characteristic function of `G_s`) equals the second norm
1730:   of `G` with spectral measure `e^(-v norm(xi)^2) mu(dxi)` (`N2GreenSq_gauss`,
1731:   every `d`, `G_s` finite for `s > 0`). Under the Fourier identity
1732:   `GreenFourier G` (`G_s hat = waveHat s`, lines 777-778) the second norm of
1733:   `G` is `N2onSq` (`N2GreenSq_eq`) and that of `p * G` is

1736:   `WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`) and, in wave L9, in `d = 1, 2, 3`

1770: Readings and narrower forms (Le's decision 2 for wave L8).
1771: - "Spatial Gaussian smoothing ... give[s] multipliers in this class" (line
1772:   845) is formalized as the membership of `e^(-eta norm(xi)^2)` in the class;
1773:   the spectral identity that the spectral measure of `p_eps * Gamma` is
1774:   `e^(-c eps norm(xi)^2) mu` is not stated (it needs Fubini against the
1775:   locally finite, infinite `Gamma`).
1776: - "Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel give[s] multipliers in this class"
1777:   is formalized as `N2GreenSq_gauss` in every `d` (transforms of measures), and
1778:   as an identity of `N2onSq` norms in every `d = 1, 2, 3`
1779:   (`damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one` and, wave L9,
1780:   `WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`).

1782:   4698) is represented by the centered Gaussian `gaussKernel v = N(0, v I)`,
1783:   the image of Mathlib's `stdGaussian` under `x -> sqrt(v) x`; every
1784:   normalization `p_eta = N(0, c eta I)` is `gaussKernel (c eta)`. The TeX does
1785:   not fix `c` in this lemma.

1787:   for the original covariance only" (lines 843-844) and "It is used after time
1788:   integration, not pointwise" (lines 911-912).

1790: Conventions and junk values. `N2GreenSq` is a complex Bochner integral (the
1791: TeX's `int G_s hat conj(G_t hat) dmu` is complex before time integration); a
1792: non-integrable integrand would give the value `0`. `N2GreenSq_gauss` and
1793: `N2GreenSq_eq` are equalities of integrals whose integrands agree almost
1794: everywhere on `(0,inf)^2` (`N2GreenOuter_gauss_ae`, `N2GreenOuter_ae_eq`), so
1795: they hold whether or not the integrands are integrable; `fourier_paper` and
1796: `fourier_one` conclude the integrability of all four outer integrands.
1797: `gaussKernel v` with `v < 0` is the Dirac mass at `0` (`sqrt v = 0`); every
1798: statement where that matters carries `v >= 0` (`gauss_waveGreen_mass` holds for
1799: every `v`). `N_0` uses `(G s univ).toReal`, which is `s` under `GreenMass`.

2056: ## FiniteGaussianMatrix (whole result)
2057: 
2058: Formalizes the finite-dimensional part of Section `S:compact-gaussian`
2059: (`notes/integrated_compact_gaussian.tex` at `a284420`): Lemma
2060: `L:gaussian-trace-bounds` (lines 47-90), Proposition
2061: `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` (lines 98-177, including the Hermitian core
2062: `E:finite-hermitian-gaussian`, line 150, and the Hermitian dilation, lines
2063: 156-169) and Remark `R:gaussian-one-variance-test` (lines 179-193). It uses
2064: two modules: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/GaussianIBP.lean`, a reusable
2065: foundation for finite Gaussian integration by parts, and
2066: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/FiniteGaussianMatrix.lean`, which contains the
2067: three results. `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is reused from
2068: `GaussianScalarPowers` (finite Hoelder, the integer-power bound, and
2069: `E Z^r <= (E Z)^r` in the bootstrap). The three results are
2070: stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by the wrappers
2071: `gaussian_trace_bounds_paper`, `finite_hermitian_gaussian_paper`,
2072: `finite_gaussian_matrix_paper` and `gaussian_one_variance_test_paper`.
2073: Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The integration by parts
2074: `E[g_k P(g)] = E[d_k P(g)]` and the integrability of polynomial moments
2075: (TeX lines 122-126) are proved, not assumed.
2076: 
2077: Abstractions and why they are faithful.
2078: - **Gaussians.** "Independent real standard Gaussians" are `g : Fin N -> Omega -> R`
2079:   on an arbitrary probability space with `iIndepFun g P` and
2080:   `HasLaw (g k) (gaussianReal 0 1) P` for every `k`.
2081:   `GaussianIBP.map_eq_stdPi` shows that their joint law is
2082:   `stdPi N = Measure.pi (fun _ => gaussianReal 0 1)`. The general theorems are
2083:   stated on `stdPi N` and transferred to the probability space through
2084:   `integral_comp_eq_stdPi`.
2085: - **One-dimensional integration by parts** comes from Mathlib's whole-line
2086:   integration by parts and the density identity `phi' = -x phi`.
2087: - **`N`-dimensional integration by parts** uses Fubini along `Fin.insertNth k`.
2088:   The partial derivative is a hypothesis on every coordinate slice.
2089: - **Matrices** are complex matrices indexed by finite types.
2090: - **`||A||_{S_p}^p = Tr((A^*A)^m)`** for `p = 2m` is `schattenPow A m`, the
2091:   real part of that trace. `schattenPow_trace` proves that the trace is real
2092:   and nonnegative, so taking the real part loses nothing.
2093:   `||A||_{S_p} = schattenNorm A m = (schattenPow A m)^(1/(2m))`.
2094: - **`|Y|` and `V^(1/2)`** are `CFC.abs Y` and `CFC.sqrt V`, the continuous
2095:   functional calculus under `MatrixOrder`. `abs_pow_even` and
2096:   `schattenNorm_sqrt` give the identities the TeX uses:
2097:   `|Y|^(2j) = Y^(2j)` and `||V^(1/2)||_{S_p}^p = Tr V^m`.
2098: - **Real traces.** The TeX compares several traces as real numbers. Lean
2099:   compares their real parts. `gaussian_trace_bounds_paper` also records
2100:   that the imaginary parts of its right-hand traces vanish; the other
2101:   wrappers state real-part bounds only, and the reality of those traces
2102:   follows from the proved matrix lemmas (`trace_psd`, `trace_mul_pow_im`).
2103: 
2104: Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
2105: - the measurability of the Gaussians (inside `HasLaw`);
2106: - the integrability of `||X||_{S_p}^p` and of `Tr Y^(2m)`, which is part of
2107:   each conclusion because the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function
2108:   is `0` in Lean;
2109: - the evenness of `p`, stated as `p = 2m` with `m >= 1` a natural number.
2110: 
2111: Every real power has a nonnegative base, so no statement holds through a
2112: junk value.

2114: Hypotheses carried but unused: `o, n, N >= 1` in
2115: `finite_gaussian_matrix_paper` (`[Nonempty o] [Nonempty n] (_hN : 1 <= N)`).
2116: The general theorem `finite_gaussian_matrix_zero` also covers the empty
2117: family `N = 0`.

2119: Proof route. The statements are the manuscript's; four steps differ from the
2120: TeX route:
2121: - The doubly stochastic step diagonalizes `D' = U^* D U` and applies Jensen's
2122:   inequality to `t^m` (`convexOn_pow`) instead of the tangent-line
2123:   inequality.
2124: - The derivative of `t -> Re Tr(B (Y + t B_k)^j)` is computed in the type
2125:   synonym `NMat n`, matrices with the L-infinity operator norm. This avoids
2126:   the product-topology diamond on `Matrix`. Polynomial growth is bounded with
2127:   the same norm.
2128: - The integration by parts is applied to real parts of traces, which are
2129:   real-valued functions.
2130: - The `m = 1` case of `E:finite-hermitian-gaussian` follows from the same

2263: ## FiniteWick (whole result)
2264: 
2265: A reusable foundation with no manuscript label of its own, proved in full with
2266: nothing supplied. It formalizes the Wick (Isserlis) step in the proof of
2267: `L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at
2268: `a284420`): the formula `E:terminal-wick-formula` (lines 3619-3622) with "each
2269: pairing has coefficient one" and "if `m+n` is odd, the expectation is zero"
2270: (line 3638), the Gaussian moment computation of the proof (lines 3662-3675), the
2271: moment bound of lines 3651-3656, and the pointwise positivity and comparison of
2272: covariance products (lines 3693-3695). The chain integrals themselves are in
2273: `TerminalWick`. Abstractions: a pairing (pair partition) of a finite set `S` of a
2274: linearly ordered finite type is a fixed-point-free involution of `S`, normalized
2275: to the identity off `S` so that each pair partition is exactly one function
2276: (`pairings`); its weight takes one factor `c(a, p a)` per pair, at the smaller
2277: element `a < p a`, so every unordered pair contributes once with coefficient one
2278: (`pairWeight`); `wickSum c S` is the sum of the weights. For `S` all of
2279: `Fin (2k)` these are the pair partitions `Pi_k` of the TeX. The double factorial
2280: is `Nat.doubleFactorial` with natural subtraction, so `(2*0-1)!! = 0!! = 1`, the
2281: empty-product convention of line 3639. Gaussian side: `stdPi N` (from
2282: `GaussianIBP`) is the law of `N` independent standard Gaussians, and Mathlib
2283: defines `multivariateGaussian 0 K` as the image of the standard Gaussian under
2284: `x -> sqrt(K) x` (`CFC.sqrt`). `CenteredGaussianField W K P` states the TeX's
2285: hypothesis "centered real Gaussian field with covariance `K`" (lines 3601-3602)
2286: as: for every finite family of points `p : Fin n -> X`, the matrix
2287: `(K(p_a, p_b))` is positive semidefinite and `(W(p_a))_a` has law
2288: `multivariateGaussian 0 (K(p_a, p_b))`. Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
2289: `K` positive semidefinite (otherwise Mathlib's `multivariateGaussian 0 K` is the
2290: Dirac mass at `0`), and every integral identity for Gaussian monomials (products
2291: of finitely many coordinates or field values) comes with the integrability of
2292: its integrand, either as a conjunct or in a separate theorem. The exception is the bridge
2293: `integral_multivariateGaussian_eq` for an arbitrary continuous `F`: it is an
2294: equality of Lean's totalized integrals and assumes no integrability, so for a
2295: non-integrable `F` (for instance `exp(x_0^4)` under a nondegenerate Gaussian)
2296: both sides are the junk value `0`; integrability transfers only through the
2297: separate equivalence `integrable_multivariateGaussian_iff`. No hypothesis is carried unused. Proof-route
2298: differences: the Gaussian identity is proved by Stein's recursion
2299: `E[g_e F(g)] = E[partial_e F(g)]` (`GaussianIBP.integral_coord_mul_eq_of_growth`)
2300: for `x = A g`, expanded along the partner of the least index
2301: (`wickSum_eq_sum_erase`), instead of differentiating the moment generating
2302: function (lines 3664-3673); the conclusion is the same. The moment bound
2303: `E(prod_{a<n} W(p_a))^2 <= (2n-1)!! V^n` (`CenteredGaussianField.sq_moment_le`)
2304: is the Wick formula for the `2n` values together with the count of `(2k-1)!!`
2305: pairings (`card_pairings_even`, `wickSum_abs_le`) and `|K(x,y)| <= V`
2306: (`CenteredGaussianField.abs_le`), instead of Hoelder's inequality and `L^(2n)`

2308: TeX step it formalizes. Junk values: `wickSum` is a finite sum, and every Bochner
2309: integral of a Gaussian monomial appears with a proof of integrability; only the
2310: continuous-`F` bridge above can equate two junk values, and the monomial
2311: results apply it to integrable monomials. Refutations
2312: (`refutations/finite-wick/`), all combinatorial or one-dimensional controls
2313: without junk-value reliance: `PairingCount` (`(2k)!/k!` pairings of a `2k`-set;

2669: ## GaussianHermite (whole result)
2670: 
2671: A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
2672: nothing is supplied. The manuscript (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
2673: at `a284420`, main TeX) uses "normalized Hermite polynomials" in three
2674: proofs: `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2517), the multiplication bound
2675: `E:occupied-multiplication` inside the proof of `P:mild-construction`
2676: (lines 1805-1810) and `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 2556-2558). It uses
2677: two facts about them: multiplication by the coordinate `g_i` acts by
2678: `g_i h_k = sqrt(k_i+1) h_(k+e_i) + sqrt(k_i) h_(k-e_i)`, and the `h_k`
2679: are orthonormal under independent standard Gaussians. The TeX takes the
2680: creation and annihilation algebra from Janson (cited at lines 2467-2468).
2681: This module proves both facts, and the spanning step of
2682: `E:occupied-multiplication`.
2683: 
2684: Formalized. The probabilists' Hermite polynomials `He_n` are Mathlib's
2685: `Polynomial.hermite` mapped to real coefficients (`hermR`, values `He`).
2686: The module proves the Appell property `He_(n+1)' = (n+1) He_n` (absent from
2687: Mathlib), the recurrences, Gaussian integration by parts on polynomials
2688: (`gE_X_mul`, from `GaussianIBP.integral_mul_eq_integral_deriv`), the shift
2689: `E[He_(n+1) q] = E[He_n q']`, and orthogonality
2690: `E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)`. The normalized `h_n = He_n/sqrt(n!)` are
2691: orthonormal (`integral_hn_mul_hn`) and satisfy
2692: `x h_n = sqrt(n+1) h_(n+1) + sqrt(n) h_(n-1)` (`mul_hn`). The products
2693: `h_k(x) = prod_i h_(k_i)(x_i)` on `R^m` are orthonormal under
2694: `GaussianIBP.stdPi m`, the product of `m` standard Gaussian laws
2695: (`integral_hk_mul_hk`), and satisfy the coordinate recurrence of the TeX
2696: (`coord_mul_hk`). The spanning step: every real polynomial in
2697: `x_1, ..., x_m` of total degree at most `n` is a real combination of the
2698: `h_l` with `|l| <= n` (`mvPolynomial_mem_hermiteSpan`, via
2699: `monomial_mem_hermiteSpan` and the triangularity `pow_mem_span1`).
2700: 
2701: Abstractions. Gaussian coordinates are the coordinate functions on
2702: `Fin m -> R` under `stdPi m`; the transfer to independent standard Gaussians
2703: on a probability space is `GaussianIBP.integral_comp_eq_stdPi`, used in
2704: `FockForm.occupied_multiplication_paper`. Multi-indices are functions
2705: `Fin m -> N`; `k - e_i` is pointwise truncated subtraction.
2706: 
2707: Junk values. None of the statements depends on one: `sqrt(n!) > 0`, every
2708: integral statement comes with its integrability, and `k - e_i` (or `n - 1`)
2709: only appears multiplied by a coefficient that vanishes exactly when the
2710: subtraction truncates: `sqrt(k_i)` (or `sqrt(n)`) in the normalized
2711: formulas, `k_i` (or `n`, as in `n * hermR (n - 1)`) in the unnormalized ones.
2712: 
2713: Not formalized here: the closed Gaussian polynomial spaces, infinitely many
2714: coordinates, and the Wiener chaos decomposition. Labelling: a row is
2715: labelled with a manuscript step only where the TeX states it (the
2716: recurrence and the orthonormality of the normalized polynomials, and the
2717: spanning step of `E:occupied-multiplication`, which the TeX uses when it
2718: passes to "finite-coordinate polynomials"); the remaining public facts are
2719: foundation rows ("no direct label") or route helpers.
2720: 
2721: Refutations (`refutations/gaussian-hermite/`, each a Lean proof that a
2722: wrong variant is false, with the package statement at the same point):
2723: `OrthogonalityNoDelta` (dropping the Kronecker delta in
2724: `E[He_n He_m] = n! delta_(nm)`), `UnnormalizedOrthonormal` (`E[He_2^2] = 2`,
2725: so the normalization is needed) and `RecurrenceNoLowering` (dropping the
2726: lowering term of `mul_hn`).

2825: ## H1Density (whole result)
2826: 
2827: A deterministic foundation of wave L7 (item L7-c), in
2828: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/H1Density.lean`: smooth compactly supported
2829: functions are dense in the weak-gradient `H^1(R^d; R)` of `WeakSobolev`. It
2830: carries no manuscript label of its own. The manuscript states the fact in one
2831: sentence in the proof of `P:spatial-four-linear`
2832: (`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at revision `a284420`, proposition
2833: lines 219-237, proof lines 239-298; the density sentence and its sketch are
2834: lines 262-266) and uses it to extend smooth-profile statements to `H^1`
2835: profiles: in the same proof at lines 270-271 ("take smooth approximants
2836: converging in `H^1`") and line 290, and in the proof of `P:spatial-energy-map`
2837: (lines 327-348) at lines 328-330 and 339. Every hypothesis is stated; nothing
2838: is supplied. In the completion module `SpatialOccupationL7Completed` it
2839: discharges the density hypothesis `hdense` of `SpatialFourLinear`
2840: (`P:spatial-four-linear` and `P:spatial-energy-map`).
2841: 
2842: - The space is the package's own `H^1` (Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces):
2843:   `WeakSobolev.IsTestFunction` (`C_c^infinity(R^d; R)`),
2844:   `WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient f g` (`int f d_v phi = -int <g, v> phi` for
2845:   every test function `phi` and direction `v`) and `WeakSobolev.MemH1`
2846:   (`f` in `L^2` with a weak gradient in `L^2`); the gradient of a smooth
2847:   function is the classical field `VariationalFloor.grad`. The approximation
2848:   is in the graph norm: `norm(phi_n - f)_2 -> 0` and
2849:   `norm(grad phi_n - g)_2 -> 0`, which is convergence in the TeX's `H^1`
2850:   norm.
2851: - `H1TestDense d` is the predicate (its body is fixed for the consumers of
2852:   wave L7); `h1TestDense d` proves it for every `d`, including `d = 0`, which
2853:   is more than the manuscript's `d = 1, 2, 3`. `exists_test_approx` is the
2854:   `eps` form and `h1TestDense_of_memH1` the `MemH1` form.
2855: - `hasWeakGradient_of_tendsto` is the converse (an `L^2` graph limit of test
2856:   functions has the limit gradient as weak gradient), so the weak-gradient
2857:   `H^1` is the closure of `C_c^infinity` in the graph norm. The manuscript
2858:   does not state it; it is used by the refutation `DropWeakGradient`.
2859: - Lean proof route (different from the TeX in order and in the
2860:   mollification step). (1) Mollify first: `mollify phi u = rho_phi * u` with
2861:   the normalized bump `rho_phi = phi.normed volume`; the `L^2` contraction
2862:   `eLpNorm_mollify_le` (Cauchy-Schwarz against the probability weight, then
2863:   Tonelli and translation invariance) and the density of continuous compactly
2864:   supported functions in `L^2` give `rho_n * u -> u` in `L^2` when the bump
2865:   radii tend to `0` (`tendsto_mollify`), where the TeX invokes `L^2`
2866:   translation continuity; the weak-gradient identity tested against
2867:   `y -> rho_phi(x - y)` gives `grad(rho_phi * f) = rho_phi * g`
2868:   (`grad_mollify`). (2) Then cut off the smooth function `h = rho * f` with

2934: ## HermiteFock (whole result)
2935: 
2936: A foundation with no manuscript label of its own; everything is proved and
2937: nothing is supplied. It is the finite Gaussian Fock layer used in
2938: `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX):
2939: the Fock half of the proof of `L:fock-form` (lines 2515-2526), the Fock
2940: sentences of the proof of `L:interval-contractions` (lines 2887-2891), the
2941: phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880),
2942: and the Hermite step of `E:occupied-multiplication` (lines 1805-1810). The
2943: TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation
2944: algebra; this module proves what is used.
2945: 
2946: Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian `L^2` space with values in a
2947: complex inner product space `X` is represented by coefficient vectors
2948: `(Fin m -> N) -> X`, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree
2949: at most `N` (`degLE m N`; `Supp N v` says `v` vanishes above degree `N`).
2950: The expansion `iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k` in the normalized
2951: Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite` links the two pictures: it is an
2952: isometry into `L^2(stdPi m; X)` (`integral_norm_sq_iota`; `stdPi m` is the
2953: law of `m` independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by `x_i` is
2954: `a_i^* + a_i` on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `sum_i x_i H_i` is
2955: the field operator `fieldOp H` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`). No tensor-product
2956: inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself,
2957: and the spatial operators `H_i` are continuous linear maps of `X`. The TeX
2958: rotates `H/||H||` to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column
2959: form with operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary. Convention: Mathlib's
2960: inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, whereas the TeX's is
2961: linear in the first slot (line 2824); every adjoint identity stated here
2962: survives the conjugation, and the norm-square and real-part identities are
2963: unchanged.
2964: 
2965: Formalized. The annihilation and creation operators
2966: `(a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i)`, `(a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i)`,
2967: the number identity `sum_i a_i^* a_i = |k|`, and the finite adjoint
2968: identity between `a_i` and `a_i^*`. The creation row from degrees `<= N` to
2969: degrees `<= N+1` has norm at most `sqrt(N+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on
2970: `u_i = a_i w` for `w` of exact degree `N+1` (`creRow_attained`). For
2971: symmetric `H_1, ..., H_m` with the column bound
2972: `sum_i ||H_i u||^2 <= c ||u||^2`, `c >= 0` (hypotheses of these lemmas, not
2973: manuscript inputs here), the field operator `sum_i (a_i^* + a_i) (x) H_i`
2974: maps degrees `<= N` to degrees `<= N+1` with norm at most
2975: `2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(c)` (`fieldOp_bound`), the same after truncation to
2976: degrees `<= N` (`fieldOp_bound_trunc`), the truncated operator is symmetric
2977: (`fieldOp_symm_trunc`), and both bounds hold in Gaussian `L^2` with
2978: integrability (`gaussian_field_bound`, `gaussian_field_bound_trunc`).
2979: Vacuum insertion: `E||sum_i g_i w_i||^2 = sum_i ||w_i||^2`
2980: (`vacuum_insertion_isometry`).
2981: 
2982: Route difference. The TeX bounds the annihilation part as the adjoint of
2983: the creation part (line 2522); Lean uses the same adjoint relation through
2984: the finite identity `sum_inner_ann` and Cauchy-Schwarz. Its annihilation
2985: theorem maps input degrees `<= N+1` to output degrees `<= N` with squared
2986: norm at most `(N+1) c`; the TeX's `sqrt(n)` (lines 1806-1809) concerns input
2987: degrees `<= n`, so the two operator domains are indexed differently, and the
2988: Fock proof says "the same bound after truncation" (lines 2522-2523). Applied
2989: to an input already supported through `N`, the `N+1`-to-`N` theorem leaves
2990: an unused degree of slack. The constant `4(N+1)c` of the sum does not need
2991: the sharper value.
2992: 
2993: Junk values. The truncated subtraction `k - e_i` occurs only multiplied by
2994: `sqrt(k_i)`, which vanishes exactly when it truncates; `c >= 0` is a
2995: hypothesis where it is used; every integral conclusion includes
2996: integrability. Coefficient vectors are arbitrary functions; only their
2997: values in degrees `<= N` (or `<= N+1`) enter the stated sums.
2998: 
2999: Not formalized here: the full Gaussian `L^2` space, infinitely many
3000: coordinates, the closed polynomial spaces and unbounded number operators.
3001: 
3002: Refutations (`refutations/hermite-fock/`): `CreRowConstant` (the constant
3003: `N` in place of `N+1` in `creRow_bound` fails at the vacuum), `NumberOrder`
3004: (`|k| + 1` in place of `|k|` in `number_identity`) and `VacuumSquareOfSum`
3005: (`(sum_i ||w_i||)^2` in place of `sum_i ||w_i||^2` in
3006: `vacuum_insertion_isometry`).

3399: ## InventoryProduct (whole result)
3400: 
3401: Formalizes `L:inventory-product` (A coefficient bound for a product with
3402: nonnegative coefficients; `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`,
3403: main file, at `a284420`: statement lines 2986-2998 with
3404: `E:inventory-product` at lines 2994-2997, proof lines 3000-3040) in full.
3405: Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis. The exponents are those fixed by the
3406: section `S:interval-upper` (line 2804) at lines 2811-2812: `nu = 3 - alpha`
3407: (`TypeContinuity.nuOf`), `beta = 4 - alpha - alpha0`
3408: (`TypeContinuity.betaOf`) and `p = 2 - alpha0` (`pOf`). The object is the
3409: actual coefficient: `v_i` and `b_{i,l}` (lines 2989-2991) are `vCoef` and
3410: `bCoef` word for word, the `i`th factor `1 + v_i z + sum_{l>=2} b_{i,l} z^l`
3411: is the Mathlib formal power series `factorSeries` (`PowerSeries.mk`), the
3412: product over `i = 1, ..., M` is `inventoryProduct` (a product over
3413: `Finset.Icc 1 M`), and `[z^k]` is `PowerSeries.coeff k`. The TeX's "finite
3414: `C = C(alpha, alpha0)`, independent of `M, k`" is the explicit real
3415: `inventoryConst alpha alpha0 = 4 e^(K(alpha, alpha0))` (`K = expConst`),
3416: which is fixed before `M` and `k` are quantified and depends on nothing else
3417: (not on `d`, `Gamma`, `mu`). `inventory_product` is the general form: for `0
3418: < alpha0 < 1` and `alpha0 + alpha < 2` (any real `alpha`), every `M` and
3419: every `k >= 1`, `[z^k] prod_{i=1}^M (...) <= C^k/(k!)^nu`.
3420: `inventory_product_paper` states it under the section's standing hypothesis
3421: `H:homog` (lines 225-242; `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0
3422: Gamma mu`) and adds `0 < C`. Only the fields `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`
3423: and `threshold` are used (through `params`: `nu >= 1`, `nu <= beta`, `beta >
3424: 2`, `p > 1`, `nu + alpha - 2 = 1`); the other fields of `H:homog` are
3425: carried and not used. The TeX's `k >= 1` is a hypothesis of every theorem
3426: that needs it; `M` ranges over all naturals (`M = 0` gives the empty
3427: product). Implicit facts made explicit: the evaluation bound `[z^k]F <=
3428: F(z)/z^k` (`coeff_prod_le_prod_tsum`) carries the summability of each factor
3429: at `z` as a hypothesis, and `inventory_product_eval_le` proves that
3430: summability at `z = theta k^nu`, `theta = 1/4`; the tail sums `sum_{i>a}
3431: i^(-s) <= a^(1-s)/(s-1)` (`sum_rpow_tail_le`, by Mathlib's sum-integral
3432: comparison) and `sum_{i>=1} i^(-s) <= s/(s-1)` (`sum_rpow_pos_le`), used in
3433: the TeX without proof, are proved. Proof-route differences (the statement is
3434: unchanged): the factors `1 + Q_i`, `Q_i = theta k i^(-p)`, are bounded by
3435: `e^(Q_i)` with `sum_i Q_i <= theta k p/(p-1)`, instead of the TeX's
3436: comparison with `int_0^inf log(1 + A x^(-p)) dx`, which gives `C k^(1/p)`
3437: (lines 3004-3011); both give the `C k` the proof needs, and no improper
3438: integral is used. The uniform bound `sum_{l>=2} P^l (1+ly)^2/(l!)^nu <= C
3439: P^2 (1+y^2)` for `0 <= P <= 1/4`, `y >= 0` (lines 3029-3030, stated without
3440: argument) is proved inside `factor_large` with `C = 128`, via `(1+ly)^2 <= 2
3441: l^2 (1+y^2)`, `l^2 <= 2^(l+1)` and `(l!)^nu >= 1`; for `i <= k`
3442: (`factor_small`) Lean assumes the singleton is at most `4P` where the TeX
3443: says `2P_i`, which is weaker and suffices for the `S_nu(4P_i)` bound.
3444: `S_nu(x) <= e^(nu x^(1/nu))` is `SeriesType.seriesNu_summable_le`. Every
3445: factor bound is first proved for each partial sum (`factor_partial_le`) and
3446: then passed to the series sum. Junk values: all real powers have positive
3447: bases (`i >= 1`, `k >= 1`, `l! >= 1`) and `k^(-1)` occurs only with `k >= 1`
3448: in every evaluation and coefficient bound (the unrestricted definitions and
3449: `factorCoeff_nonneg` also cover zero indices with Lean's conventions, used by
3450: no bound), and every `tsum` (`factorEval`) comes with its summability, so
3451: no junk value enters a conclusion. Nothing in the lemma is left
3452: unformalized, and no conclusion is narrower than the TeX's. The use of the
3453: lemma in the proof of `P:interval-coefficients` (lines 3537, 3546) is not
3454: part of this section (see `IntervalScalar`; `IntervalScalarCompleted`
3455: connects `inventory_product` to the input `hinv` of that proof).

2940: sentences of the proof of `L:interval-contractions` (lines 2887-2891), the
2941: phase insertion on a color in its vacuum (lines 2838-2841 and 2878-2880),

2943: TeX cites Janson (lines 2467-2468) for the creation and annihilation
2944: algebra; this module proves what is used.

2946: Model (decision 5 of wave L9). The Gaussian `L^2` space with values in a
2947: complex inner product space `X` is represented by coefficient vectors
2948: `(Fin m -> N) -> X`, indexed by multi-indices, restricted to total degree
2949: at most `N` (`degLE m N`; `Supp N v` says `v` vanishes above degree `N`).
2950: The expansion `iota N v (x) = sum_(|k| <= N) h_k(x) v_k` in the normalized
2951: Hermite functions of `GaussianHermite` links the two pictures: it is an
2952: isometry into `L^2(stdPi m; X)` (`integral_norm_sq_iota`; `stdPi m` is the
2953: law of `m` independent standard Gaussians), multiplication by `x_i` is
2954: `a_i^* + a_i` on coefficients (`coord_smul_iota`), and `sum_i x_i H_i` is
2955: the field operator `fieldOp H` (`sum_coord_smul_iota`). No tensor-product
2956: inner product is used: the "other Hilbert factor" of the TeX is `X` itself,
2957: and the spatial operators `H_i` are continuous linear maps of `X`. The TeX
2958: rotates `H/||H||` to a first coordinate (line 1805); the general column
2959: form with operators `H_i` makes that step unnecessary. Convention: Mathlib's
2960: inner product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, whereas the TeX's is
2961: linear in the first slot (line 2824); every adjoint identity stated here
2962: survives the conjugation, and the norm-square and real-part identities are
2963: unchanged.

2966: `(a_i v)_k = sqrt(k_i+1) v_(k+e_i)`, `(a_i^* v)_k = sqrt(k_i) v_(k-e_i)`,

2968: identity between `a_i` and `a_i^*`. The creation row from degrees `<= N` to
2969: degrees `<= N+1` has norm at most `sqrt(N+1)` (`creRow_bound`), attained on

4393: `{cos(rho t), sin(rho t)}`, the bound `E:masked-trig-products`,
4394: `||1_I A P_r Q_rho||_a^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)`, with
4395: `Q_h` as in `E:masked-frequency-pair` and `<x> = sqrt(1+x^2)`. All four
4396: `cos`/`sin` combinations are covered, together with every step of the
4397: proof: the four-mode expansion (coefficients of absolute value `1/4`,
4398: frequencies `+-r +- rho`), the Hilbert-space inequality
4399: `||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2`, and the frequency

4402: the complexified temporal completion `H_a^C` of `L:masked-time-completion`,

4404: `E` stands for that completion (for the concrete completion see
4405: `TimeCompletion`; a complex inner product space in the

7776: ## VariationalDilation (whole result)
7777: 
7778: Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-control-dilation` (Radon and Rayleigh
7779: dilation; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines 225-268 at
7780: `a284420`) together with the definitions it uses, in two modules:
7781: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WeakSobolev.lean` (a hand-built real Sobolev
7782: space and the real Rayleigh value set) and
7783: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalDilation.lean` (the control class,
7784: the dilation, the mean, variance, rate and integrated rate, and the lemma).
7785: The wrapper `variational_control_dilation_paper` states the lemma with the
7786: section's standing hypotheses (line 4: a nonzero covariance satisfying
7787: `H:homog`, modelled by `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance`, with `a = alpha0`):
7788: for `r > 0`, `D_r` is a bijection of the class with inverse `D_(1/r)`, and the
7789: four identities of `E:variational-dilation-values` hold. Nothing is supplied as
7790: a hypothesis.
7791: 
7792: Abstractions and why they are faithful.
7793: The class `E:variational-positive-class` (lines 5-10) consists of smooth
7794: functions on `R x R^d` with compact support inside `(0,1) x R^d`, i.e. elements
7795: of `C_c^infinity((0,1) x R^d)` extended by zero. `CPos_nonempty` proves that
7796: the class is nonempty (lines 13-17) using a different bump. The mean
7797: `h_{Psi,s}` and the variance `v_Psi` are the
7798: displays `E:compact-raw-mean` and `E:compact-raw-cost`
7799: (`notes/integrated_compact_mean_family.tex` lines 402-412), with
7800: `(Gamma * phi)(x) = int phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)` and `int_0^1` taken over
7801: `Ioo 0 1`. Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces, so `WeakSobolev` defines
7802: `H^1(R^d; R)` by weak gradients (`int f d_v phi = -int <g,v> phi` for every
7803: test function `phi` and direction `v`). It proves that an `L^2` weak gradient
7804: is unique a.e. (`weakGradient_ae_unique`), so a Rayleigh set built from pairs
7805: `(f, g)` is the manuscript's set of `f`.
7806: 
7807: The rate `lambda_{Psi,s}` is defined in Lean by the real Rayleigh form
7808: `E:variational-real-rayleigh`: `rate = sqrt(sSup R_s)`, where `R_s` is the set
7809: of values `int h_s f^2 - ||grad f||_2^2` over unit `f in H^1(R^d; R)`. The
7810: manuscript's primary definition is `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`, with `E_s` the
7811: spectral bottom of the self-adjoint `-Delta - h_s` on `H^2`. The manuscript
7812: proves that the two agree (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`), but that equality is
7813: **not formalized**, because it needs unbounded self-adjoint operators and
7814: spectral theory. Likewise `v_Psi` is the integral form of
7815: `E:compact-raw-cost`, and its identification with `E W(Psi)^2`
7816: (`L:compact-raw-profile`, which needs the Gaussian noise) is **not
7817: formalized**. The TeX proof itself works with exactly these two forms
7818: (Lebesgue substitution in the pairing, and the real Rayleigh bijection).
7819: 
7820: Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
7821: - A Rayleigh trial must have `h_s f^2` integrable. The condition keeps
7822:   Lean's junk value `0` for a non-integrable integral out of the set. For
7823:   the manuscript's `h_s` (`Psi in CPos`, `s in [0,1]`) it is automatic:
7824:   `VariationalMean.isRayleighTrial_mean_iff_paper` proves that a trial is
7825:   then exactly a unit `f in L^2` with an `L^2` weak gradient, because `h_s`
7826:   is bounded and continuous (`L:variational-global-mean`, formalized in
7827:   `VariationalMean`).
7828: - `Psi` is continuous; this follows from smoothness.
7829: - The identities hold for every real `s`, not only for `s in [0,1]`.
7830: 
7831: Junk values. Every identity is an exact identity of Bochner integrals and of
7832: `sSup`. It would remain true if an integrand were not integrable, or if the
7833: Rayleigh set were empty or unbounded (Lean's value `0` on both sides). The
7834: companion does not exclude these junk cases. It proves only conditional
7835: transfers, in `variational_control_dilation_integrable_paper`:
7836: - every integrand in the definitions of `h`, `v` and `I` is integrable for
7837:   `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`;
7838: - the Rayleigh sets themselves scale, so a Rayleigh set is nonempty and
7839:   bounded above for `D_r Psi` exactly when it is for `Psi`.
7840: 
7841: So if a quantity is a genuine integral or supremum for `Psi`, the identity
7842: relates it to a genuine integral or supremum for `D_r Psi`. For
7843: `s in [0,1]`, `VariationalMean` proves that the integrand of `h_s(x)` is
7844: integrable and that `h_s` is bounded (`L:variational-global-mean`,
7845: `variational_global_mean_paper`), so the mean identity relates genuine
7846: integrals there. That the variance and rate integrands are integrable, and
7847: that the Rayleigh sets are nonempty and bounded above, is not proved in
7848: this module. For `Psi in C_pos` under the section's hypotheses these are
7849: proved in `VariationalRate` (`rawCost_genuine`, `unmasked_rate`); the
7850: identifications `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2` and `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` remain
7851: outside Lean. The
7852: integrability equivalences are Lean-route auxiliaries: the TeX proof
7853: (lines 243-250) works with nonnegative integrands and Tonelli and states none
7854: of them. Their rows below say so.
7855: 
7856: The TeX's square-root step uses positivity of the rates. Lean instead uses
7857: `sqrt(sSup(r^2 S)) = r sqrt(sSup S)`, which holds for every set `S`.
7858: 
7859: Hypotheses carried but unused: `Gamma != 0`, and every clause of `H:homog`
7860: except the set scaling. The general theorems assume only the set scaling
7861: `SetScaling` and continuity of `Psi`.
7862: 
7863: Not formalized:
7864: - `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)` (`P:variational-unmasked-rate`; positivity of the
7865:   Rayleigh-form rate is in `VariationalRate`);
7866: - `v_Psi = E W(Psi)^2` (`L:compact-raw-profile`; finiteness and positivity
7867:   of the integral form are in `VariationalRate`);
7868: - the mixed-derivative bounds of `L:variational-global-mean` (its display
7869:   is formalized in `VariationalMean`);
7870: - integrability of the integrands of `v` and `I` (that of `h` for
7871:   `s in [0,1]` is in `VariationalMean`), and nonemptiness and
7872:   boundedness of the Rayleigh sets (only their transfer under `D_r` is
7873:   proved);
7874: - the TeX's side remark that `U_r` preserves `H^2` and that
7875:   `H_{D_r Psi,s} U_r = r^2 U_r H_{Psi,s}` (not part of the statement).
7876: 
7877: The auxiliary definition `VariationalDilation.dilHomeo` (the spatial dilation
7878: as a homeomorphism of `R x R^d`) only names a map used in the proof and has no
7879: row. The structure fields `IsRayleighTrial.memLp_f`, `memLp_g`, `weakGrad`,
7880: `unit` and `integrable_pot` are projections of `IsRayleighTrial` and have no
7881: rows either. Four refutations in `refutations/variational-dilation/` prove
7882: that the following wrong variants are false:
7883: - the mean scaling with `r` in place of `r^2`;
7884: - the variance scaling without the Lebesgue factor (`r^(d+4-alpha)`);
7885: - the rate scaling with `r^2`;
7886: - the bijection with `r > 0` dropped.

7949: ## VariationalFloor (whole result)
7950: 
7951: Five deterministic foundations of wave L6 (item L6-d), in
7952: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalFloor.lean`. They carry no
7953: manuscript label of their own: they are the facts that the variational rates
7954: of `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` (Section
7955: `S:unmasked-variational`) and the spatial results of
7956: `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (Section
7957: `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`) use, at revision `a284420`. Every
7958: hypothesis is stated; nothing is supplied. They are consumed by
7959: `VariationalRate`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls` and
7960: `SpatialOccupationCompleted`.
7961: 
7962: - (F1) `dilation_floor`, `rayleighSet_floor`: the dilation floor. For a
7963:   nonzero locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling
7964:   `Gamma(c A) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` of `H:homog` and `alpha < 2`, and a
7965:   continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `z` with
7966:   `y -> z(x-y)` `Gamma`-integrable for every `x` (so `Gamma * z` is a genuine
7967:   integral, not Lean's junk value `0`), one unit test `f` in `C_c^infinity`,
7968:   an `L^2` weak gradient `g` and one `eps > 0` give
7969:   `eps <= int V f^2 - int norm(g)^2` for every potential `V >= Gamma * z` with
7970:   `V f^2` integrable. The test is `U_l phi / norm(phi)_2` for a fixed bump
7971:   `phi` and small `l`; the potential term is at least
7972:   `l^alpha (int z) Gamma(closed unit ball)/norm(phi)_2^2` (Tonelli in
7973:   `(x, y)` and the scaling of `Gamma` on balls) and the gradient term is
7974:   `l^2 norm(grad phi)_2^2/norm(phi)_2^2`. It is a pure inequality (no limit,
7975:   no supremum). This is the elementary scaling principle behind the
7976:   positivity in `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (TeX lines 150-155), which the
7977:   manuscript obtains instead from the compact trial of
7978:   `P:compact-original-common-trial`; it also discharges the input
7979:   `RayleighFloor` of `SpatialStaticControls`.
7980: - (F2) `measure_ball_pos`, `measure_closedBall_pos`: `Gamma(B_r) > 0` for
7981:   every `r > 0` when `Gamma != 0` has the set scaling (exhaustion by balls
7982:   and scaling: the argument of `L:spatial-static-controls`, occupation file
7983:   lines 89-91).
7984: - (F3) `autocorr_nonneg_of_posDef`: for a real `Q` in `C_c^infinity`,
7985:   `int c_Q dGamma >= 0` when `Gamma` is positive definite in the sense of the
7986:   field `Gamma_posdef` of `H:homog`, where `c_Q = SpatialFourierBound.autocorr Q`
7987:   (`c_Q(y) = int Q(x) Q(x-y) dx`, the inner integral of `B_Gamma(Q,Q)` in
7988:   `E:spatial-physical-pair`); route: `HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap` and the
7989:   cast of the real pairing to `C`. `autocorr_pos`: `int c_Q dGamma > 0` for
7990:   continuous, nonnegative, nonzero, compactly supported `Q` and nonzero
7991:   locally finite `Gamma` with the set scaling (no positive definiteness; TeX
7992:   lines 88-91 and 182-185 of the occupation file).
7993: - (F4) `hasWeakGradient_of_test`, with the gradient field `grad`: a test
7994:   function has its classical gradient as weak gradient
7995:   (`WeakSobolev.HasWeakGradient`).
7996: - (F5) `ae_eq_zero_of_hasWeakGradient_zero`: for `d >= 1`, an `L^2` function
7997:   with weak gradient `0` is `0` almost everywhere (half (b) of the D8-lite foundation; half (a),
7998:   the density of test functions in the weak-gradient `H^1`, is
7999:   `H1Density.h1TestDense`, wave L7). This is the fact used in `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (occupation
8000:   file lines 180-182); the Lean route differs from the TeX's Fourier-support
8001:   argument: the mollifications `rho_n * f` are smooth with derivative
8002:   `(D rho_n) * f = 0`, hence constant, they converge to `f` almost everywhere,
8003:   and a nonzero constant is not in `L^2(R^d)` for `d >= 1`. The hypothesis
8004:   `d >= 1` is necessary (refutation `ZeroDimension`).
8005: 
8006: Also `integral_pos_of_pos_zero` and `conv_pos` (positivity of integrals
8007: against such `Gamma`, from F2), and `exists_radius_fn`. Junk values: the
8008: statements involving `conv Gamma z` assume the integrability of
8009: `y -> z(x-y)`; the F3 integral is a genuine integral for locally finite
8010: `Gamma` (`SpatialFourierBound.integrable_autocorr`); the floor's conclusion
8011: is about the Rayleigh value of one explicit trial, not about a supremum.
8012: Lemmas labelled "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)" serve
8013: only the Lean proofs and are not TeX steps.

8058: 
8059: Formalizes Lemma `L:variational-heat-envelope` (Gaussian envelope for the
8060: original covariance; `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` at `a284420`,
8061: statement lines 23-35, proof 37-62) in full, and the display
8062: `E:variational-global-mean` of Lemma `L:variational-global-mean` (global
8063: regularity of the original mean; statement 64-74, proof 76-96), in
8064: `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/VariationalMean.lean`. It reuses the definitions
8065: of `VariationalDilation`: the convolution `conv` (`(Gamma * phi)(x) = int
8066: phi(x-y) Gamma(dy)`), the mean `mean` (`h_{Psi,s}`, `E:compact-raw-mean`) and
8067: the control class `CPos` (`E:variational-positive-class`). The only new
8068: manuscript object is the heat kernel `heatK eps x = (2 pi eps)^(-d/2)
8069: e^(-norm(x)^2/(2 eps))` (lines 25-26). Nothing is supplied as a hypothesis.
8070: 
8071: The wrappers state the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-5: a nonzero
8072: covariance satisfying `H:homog`, with `a = alpha0`) as
8073: `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu` and `Gamma != 0`;
8074: the mean is taken with exponent `alpha0`.
8075: `variational_heat_envelope_paper` (with `eps > 0`) gives, for every `x`, the
8076: integrability of `y -> p_eps(x-y)` against `Gamma` (so `(Gamma * p_eps)(x)`,

8078: integrand against `mu`, the identity of `E:variational-heat-envelope` as

8080: (Gamma * p_eps)(0)`, and `(Gamma * p_eps)(0) > 0`.
8081: `variational_global_mean_paper` (with `Psi in CPos`) gives real
8082: `M, C_Psi >= 0` with `0 <= h_s(x) <= M` and `|h_s(x) - h_t(x)| <= C_Psi
8084: display, stated pointwise in `x`). It also gives the integrability of every

8100: `(Gamma * p_eps)(0)` and of `h_s(x)` is stated as integrability of the

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩

    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/

803	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   804	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
   805	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
   806	  in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
   807	  $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
   808	  \[
   809	    N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
   810	    N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
   811	    N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
   812	    \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
   813	  \]
   814	  Let
   815	  \[
   816	    K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   817	    \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   818	  \]
   819	  Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
   820	  $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   821	  $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   822	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   823	    N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   824	    N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   825	  \end{equation}
   826	  More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   827	  $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   828	  by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   829	  $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   830	  and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   831	  \[
   832	    K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   833	    \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   834	  \]
   835	  Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   836	  \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   837	    \begin{split}
   838	      0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   839	      0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   840	    \end{split}
   841	  \end{equation}
   842	  These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
   843	  domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
   844	  scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
   845	  Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
   846	  give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
   847	  unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
   848	\end{lemma}
  2472	\begin{lemma}[Gaussian cutoff form bound]\label{L:fock-form}
  2473	  Retain the covariance and $R_\alpha$ of Section~\ref{S:static-phase}. Fix
  2474	  $\epsilon > 0$. Represent the smoothed real field on independent standard
  2475	  Gaussian coordinates as $W_\epsilon(x) = \sum_{i\ge1}g_i e_i(x)$ in
  2476	  $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $P_N$ be projection onto Gaussian Hermite degrees at most
  2477	  $N$, and $S_b$ spatial Fourier projection onto $|\eta| \le b$. For finite $m$,
  2478	  on their joint range set
  2479	  \[
  2480	    B_{N,m,b}=P_NS_b\Big(\sum_{i=1}^m g_i M_{e_i}\Big)S_bP_N,\qquad
  2481	    A_\rho=\rho^2-\Delta .
  2482	  \]
  2483	  These are bounded selfadjoint operators and, uniformly in $\epsilon,m,b$,
  2484	  \begin{equation}\label{E:fock-sandwich}
  2485	    \|A_\rho^{-1/2}B_{N,m,b}A_\rho^{-1/2}\|

  2531	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2532	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2533	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2534	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2535	  \[
  2536	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  2537	  \]
  2538	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  2539	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2540	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2541	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2542	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2543	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2544	    \begin{split}
  2545	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2546	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2547	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2548	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2549	    \end{split}
  2550	  \end{equation}
  2551	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2552	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2553	\end{lemma}
  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}
  3638	  Each pairing has coefficient one. If $m+n$ is odd, the expectation is zero.
  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If
  3640	  $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently,
  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
  3642	  finite partial-order second moments in the same direction. The series
  3643	  $\sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$ for every real or complex
  3644	  $r$.
  3645	\end{lemma}
  3703	\begin{lemma}[Uniform series tails from scaled moments]\label{L:uniform-series-tail}
  3704	  Fix $(T,x)$. For each positive regularization pair $(\epsilon,\delta)$, let
  3705	  $Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$ be the terms of Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick} for a
  3706	  field with nonnegative covariance. Write $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r) =
  3707	  \sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n^{\epsilon,\delta}$. Suppose that, for some $r > 1$ and
  3708	  finite $B_r$,
  3709	  \[
  3710	    \sup_{\epsilon,\delta>0}
  3711	    \E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(r)|^2\le B_r,
  3712	    \qquad
  3713	    Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\longrightarrow X_n
  3714	    \text{ in }L^2\text{ for each fixed }n.
  3715	  \]
  3716	  Then $u = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$,
  3717	  $u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1) \to u$ in $L^2$, and
  3718	  \begin{equation}\label{E:uniform-series-tail}
  3719	    \|Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\|_2,\ \|X_n\|_2
  3720	    \le B_r^{1/2}r^{-n},\qquad
  3721	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}Y_n^{\epsilon,\delta}\right\|_2,
  3722	    \left\|\sum_{n>N}X_n\right\|_2
  3723	    \le\frac{B_r^{1/2}r^{-(N+1)}}{1-r^{-1}}.
  3724	  \end{equation}
  3725	  If also $\E|u^{\epsilon,\delta}(1)|^2 \le B_1$ uniformly, then $\E|u|^2 \le
  3726	  B_1$.
  3727	\end{lemma}
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}

    65	  \label{L:variational-global-mean}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int

(manuscript revision ba01d98): "The strict intervals are nonempty."

module

public import Mathlib.Tactic

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.DriverParameters

/-- The parameter part of Hypothesis `H:homog`, with `a = α₀`. -/
def Homog (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) ∧ 0 < a ∧ a < 1 ∧ a + alpha < 2 ∧
    ((0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1))

/-- The `γ`-interval `0 < γ < min(1/2, (2-α)/2)` is nonempty. -/
theorem gamma_interval_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    ∃ γ : ℝ, 0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2) := by
  obtain ⟨-, ha0, -, hthr, -⟩ := h
  have hm : 0 < min (1 / 2 : ℝ) ((2 - alpha) / 2) :=
    lt_min (by norm_num) (by linarith)
  exact ⟨min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2) / 2, by linarith, by linarith⟩

/-- The `(θ, β)`-interval `1/2 < θ < β < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-α)/2)` is nonempty. -/
theorem theta_beta_interval_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    ∃ θ β : ℝ, 1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2) := by
  obtain ⟨-, -, ha1, hthr, -⟩ := h
  set m := min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2) with hm
  have hm' : 1 / 2 < m := lt_min (by linarith) (by linarith)
  exact ⟨1 / 2 + (m - 1 / 2) / 3, 1 / 2 + 2 * (m - 1 / 2) / 3,
    by linarith, by linarith, by linarith⟩

/-- `E:driver-parameters`: "The strict intervals are nonempty", i.e. there are
`γ, θ, β` with `0 < γ < min(1/2, (2-α)/2)` and
`1/2 < θ < β < min(1 - a/2, (3-a-α)/2)`. -/
theorem parameters_nonempty (d : ℕ) (alpha a : ℝ) (h : Homog d alpha a) :
    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - a / 2) ((3 - a - alpha) / 2)) := by
  obtain ⟨γ, hγ⟩ := gamma_interval_nonempty d alpha a h
  obtain ⟨θ, β, hθβ⟩ := theta_beta_interval_nonempty d alpha a h
  exact ⟨γ, θ, β, hγ, hθβ⟩

end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.DriverParameters

/-- The growth exponent `κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α)` of `E:kappa`. -/
noncomputable def kappa (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) : ℝ := (4 - alpha - alpha0) / (3 - alpha)

/-- `E:kappa`: under the parameter assumptions of Hypothesis `H:homog`,
`1 < κ < 2`. -/
theorem kappa_mem_Ioo (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3)
    (h0 : 0 < alpha0) (h1 : alpha0 < 1) (hthr : alpha0 + alpha < 2)
    (halpha : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)) :
    kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 := by
  have hd3 : (d : ℝ) ≤ 3 := by
    rcases hd with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  have h3 : alpha < 3 := by
    rcases halpha with ⟨_, h⟩ | ⟨h, rfl⟩
    · linarith
    · rw [h]; norm_num
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 3 - alpha := by linarith
  unfold kappa
  constructor
  · rw [lt_div_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
  · rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
